record.paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
record.original_question: For dispersing billiards with small holes, can one give a rigorous formulation of the proposed small-hole escape-rate expansion in which the exponential escape rate, including the differential escape rate for two holes A and B, is expressed through a series of correlation functions of zero-mean phase functions associated with the holes under the billiard collision map F?

evidence.quote: the exponential escape rate γ as above can be expanded in powers of the hole size h using series of correlation functions, as can the differential escape rate of one vs two holes.
Open problem 8. Give a rigorous formulation of the escape rate of dispersing billiards with small holes along the lines of Eq. (9).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q\subset\mathbb{T}^2$ be a planar dispersing (Sinai) billiard table with $C^3$ smooth, strictly convex scatterers having pairwise disjoint closures and satisfying the finite-horizon condition. Let $F:M\to M$ denote the associated collision map on the phase space $M=\partial Q\times[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$ with coordinates $(r,\varphi)$, and let $\mu$ denote the smooth invariant (SRB) measure $d\mu=c\cos\varphi\,dr\,d\varphi$.

For a measurable subset $H\subset M$ (a "hole"), let $M_n(H)=\{x\in M:F^k x\notin H,\ 0\le k\le n\}$ be the set of orbits surviving up to time $n$, and define the exponential escape rate
$$\gamma(H)=-\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log\mu(M_n(H)),$$
when the limit exists.

Consider a one-parameter family of holes $H=H_h$ shrinking with parameter $h\to 0^+$ (so $\mu(H_h)\to 0$). Let $\mathbf{1}_{H}$ be the indicator of the hole and $\psi_H=\mathbf{1}_H-\mu(H)$ be the associated zero-mean phase function. Heuristically, one expects an expansion of the form
$$\gamma(H_h)=\mu(H_h)\Bigl(1-\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{\mu(H_h)}\int_M \psi_{H_h}(\psi_{H_h}\circ F^n)\,d\mu+\text{higher order}\Bigr),$$
and similarly for the differential escape rate $\gamma(A\cup B)-\gamma(A)-\gamma(B)$ of two disjoint holes $A,B$ expressed through cross-correlations $\int \psi_A(\psi_B\circ F^n)\,d\mu$.

Problem: Give a rigorous formulation and proof of such a small-hole asymptotic expansion of the exponential escape rate $\gamma(H_h)$ (and of the differential escape rate for two holes $A$ and $B$) for finite-horizon dispersing billiards under the collision map $F$, expressing the coefficients as convergent series of correlation functions of the zero-mean phase functions associated with the holes.
artifact.status_search_result: Existence of escape rates and conditionally invariant measures for dispersing billiards with small holes is established (Demers–Wright–Young and related work), but a rigorous small-hole power-series expansion of the escape rate (and differential escape rate for pairs of holes) in terms of correlation series for the billiard collision map does not appear in the literature; the problem is stated as an open problem in surveys on open billiards.

status_evidence.title: Escape Rates and Physically Relevant Measures for Billiards with Small Holes
status_evidence.snippet: Proves existence of a common escape rate and limiting conditionally invariant distribution for dispersing billiards with small holes; escape rate characterized via pressure on the survivor set.
status_evidence.claim: Existence and basic properties of the escape rate are established, but no rigorous correlation-series expansion in hole size is given.

status_evidence.title: Dispersing Billiards with Small Holes
status_evidence.snippet: Survey chapter on open dispersing billiards summarizing escape-rate results and Young-tower techniques.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art results stop short of providing the proposed small-hole power-series expansion of gamma in terms of correlation functions.
